newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to ask bids on railway project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to ask bids on railway project.

text.p: Taiwan will invite local and foreign companies on Wednesday to bid for the island's planned T$441.9 billion, high-speed railway project, a Communications Ministry official said on Tuesday.

Companies showing healthy operations during the past three years with a minimum paid-in capital of T$10 billion or an annual sales revenue of T$30 billion would be qualified to apply for the project, said the ministry official.
Small companies with a minimum T$2 billion paid-in capital can also form an alliance to take part in the project if together they can raise a paid-in capital of T$10 billion.
Taiwan approved a bill in 1994 to allow private firms for the first time to invest in the island's railway construction projects.
To encourage investments, the bill awards tax concessions and loans to private firms that work on railway projects.
The government plans to attract 40 percent of the T$441.9 billion funding from private interests.
The 345-km (220 miles) railway, connecting northern Taipei and southern Kaohsiung, is scheduled for completion in 2003.
Companies from France, Germany and Japan have all voiced interest in participating in the project.
Application forms are available at the Communications Ministry between October 30 and December 31. The deadline for applying is January 15, 1997.
